name: Carne en su Jugo Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified on the card at 620 cal / 58g protein per serving at 6 servings, the single highest protein density in this slice, and it needs no rice base to get there. Jalisco classic that nobody on the site has seen. Tomatillos are board-tracked. Confidence: high, nutrition read off the recipe card. | HARVEST: Last four lines are the source's optional toppings section.
OVERRIDE Yellow Onion: 'Chopped white onion' topping, no qty
intro_html: Carne en su jugo translates to meat in its own juice, and that is exactly the technique. Thin sliced steak simmers in a tomatillo and jalapeno salsa with crisped bacon and beans until the whole thing turns into a brothy bowl that eats like a stew. It is a Jalisco classic and the highest protein dish in this batch by a wide margin. Each bowl carries 69 grams of protein and 770 calories for about $5.00.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, ground cumin, black pepper): ~$0.29. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $70.06 across 14 servings, so roughly $5.00 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $79.64 across 14 servings, roughly $5.69 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.80 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $86.44. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $5.00 a bowl. Beans and bacon do a lot of the lifting here, which is why a bowl with this much protein in it does not cost more.
shop_smart: Tomatillos are cheapest in season and at Latin groceries, where they are often sold loose by the pound rather than in a shrink wrapped tray.
Canned beans are the right call for a batch this size. Dried beans are cheaper still if you plan ahead, but canned keeps the cook to one afternoon.
Bacon ends and pieces work perfectly since everything gets chopped anyway. Where a store sells them, they cost far less than sliced bacon.
Cilantro goes in by the bunch, twice, in the salsa and on top. Buy two bunches and store them stems down in water in the fridge.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and cook it in a large pot until crisp. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat behind.
Slice the steak thin against the grain, season it with salt, cumin, and black pepper, and sear it in the bacon fat in batches until just browned.
Husk and rinse the tomatillos, then blend them with the jalapenos, most of the cilantro, and the garlic into a rough green salsa.
Pour the salsa into the pot, scraping up everything stuck to the bottom, and simmer 10 minutes until it darkens slightly.
Return the beef with enough water to make it brothy, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the meat is tender.
Drain and rinse the beans and stir them in, then cook 5 more minutes so they warm through and pick up the salsa.
Finish each bowl with the crisped bacon, chopped raw onion, and the remaining cilantro.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Ladle that weight into each of 14 containers, stirring between scoops so the beans and beef split evenly, and keep the bacon and raw onion in a separate bag so they stay crisp. Each bowl lands at 770 calories with 69 grams of protein.

head.description: Carne en su jugo meal prep: thin sliced steak simmered in a tomatillo and jalapeno salsa with bacon and beans, Jalisco style. 770 calories, 69g protein, about $5.00 per serving.
head.keywords: carne en su jugo, jalisco beef, tomatillo beef stew, beef and bean bowls, budget meal prep, mexican recipes
recipeIngredient: 5.75 lb beef flank or sirloin steak
steps: Crisp the chopped bacon and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Sear the thin sliced seasoned steak in the bacon fat in batches.
Blend tomatillos, jalapenos, cilantro, and garlic into a green salsa and simmer it in the pot.
Return the beef with water and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, then stir in the beans.
Top with bacon, raw onion, and cilantro and portion into 14 containers.
